description: Universal rules for consuming, applying, and incrementally extending Brand Packs from a client-owned brand folder.

rules.rule: Validate the resolved Brand Pack before creating or reviewing output. Stop when files, slugs, versions, schemas, or hashes diverge.

Resolve Brand Packs as direct slug-named children of one folder named brand. The folder may be a saved user library or a project-local override, but it must never live inside .ai, .codex, .claude, the plugin source, or the plugin cache.

When no usable brand folder is resolved or the saved absolute path is stale, ask the user for the absolute path to the downloaded folder named brand, persist it through config set, and stop branded work until the folder reports ready. Never require a copy inside the current project.
Discover valid Brand Pack siblings dynamically on every command. Persist only the brand folder path, never a slug list, so newly added packs require no configuration update.

Never scaffold, clone, rename, or synthesize a missing Brand Pack. New packs must be produced by the authorized Brand Portal/Vox workflow and added as direct siblings inside the configured brand folder.

For >>brand {slug}, use the first token as the slug. Without a slug, auto-detect only when the resolved brand folder contains exactly one valid Brand Pack; otherwise list installed slugs and require a selection.
Treat brand.source.json, tokens.json, build-manifest.json, and the optional client-owned brand.rules.json as technical sources. Use HTML only as a visual reference.
Keep the plugin universal. Never add a client name, token, asset, copy, feedback, or client-specific rule to the plugin source or cache.
Never edit brand.source.json, tokens.json, brand-guidelines.md, design-system.html, build-manifest.json, or pack-managed assets and references. They are immutable downloaded artifacts.
Persist accepted client feedback only in <brand-folder>/{slug}/brand.rules.json through the learn command. Keep its revision independent from the immutable Brand Pack version.
Do not turn every correction into a lasting rule. Write only when the user explicitly requests a permanent brand preference or confirms permanence after clarification.
Load all active client rules applicable to the requested surface before creating or reviewing output. Re-run context immediately after a rule is learned or changed.
Preserve brand.rules.json and references/feedback/ when the immutable Brand Pack is upgraded or reinstalled. Plugin upgrades must never mutate either client-owned path.

Treat Brand Runtime updates and Brand Pack updates as different operations. A request to update Brand Runtime must never replace, merge, regenerate, or edit a Brand Pack, its saved folder path, brand.rules.json, or references/feedback/.

When the user asks the agent to update Brand Runtime, detect the active host from the session context, run that host's native marketplace refresh and plugin update commands, and verify the installed version. Show commands without executing only when the user requested instructions.

After updating Brand Runtime, state that the running session still uses its previously loaded plugin until Claude Code runs /reload-plugins or the user starts a new session. Never claim the update is active in the current session before that boundary.
By default, use only declared tokens and assets, preserve their proportions and themes, and do not invent values, variants, or states. Local icon extensions follow only icon-extension-guardrail.

Before composing cards, definition blocks, capabilities, states, or editorial notes, inventory declared iconography and map each asset to a real semantic function. Prefer a compatible official icon over leader lines, initials, or decorative markers.

Create an output-local icon only with explicit user authorization and when the pack declares enough family construction guidance, such as viewBox, stroke, fill, scale, or container. Keep the extension outside the Brand Pack, identify it as non-canonical, and report a conflict when the family cannot be preserved.
For interfaces, prefer semantic theme roles over primitive values and never invent missing states, colors, or families.

Before implementation, map page or canvas margins, section gaps, component insets, and internal stack gaps to declared layout.spacing tokens. Reuse those relationships consistently and never invent a one-off distance to make a single frame pass.

Text-bearing containers must size from content by default. Fixed block dimensions are allowed only when the surface requires them and rendered text at every target size, after fonts load and wrapping stabilizes, remains inside the declared padding. Never conceal authored content with clipping, masking, hidden overflow, or line clamping unless truncation is explicitly requested and visibly communicated.

Rendered QA must verify both containment and inset preservation: text and child bounds plus scroll dimensions stay inside each container, and wrapping does not consume the mapped bottom or trailing-edge spacing at any required breakpoint or export size.
Load the requested surface rules before implementing a site, product interface, presentation, or document.

The skill may be distributed through runtime adapters, but Brand Packs remain in the resolved client-owned brand folder. Runtime entry points and plugin caches never receive editable copies of a pack.
For documents and presentations, preserve the complete content and global order. Source pagination is not binding unless the user explicitly requests it.
Do not impose a closed template catalog, one universal grid, or identical page anatomy. Use brand tokens and compose each block according to its editorial function.

Cards, dividers, and callouts must encode real grouping, comparison, status, or emphasis. Do not default to a rounded surface with a colored left rule; test an icon plus title, editorial typography, data treatment, or a plain note first.

For HTML documents, choose continuous flow or a paginated page canvas according to reading and export needs. When paginated, derive width and height from the target format or source ratio, share geometry between the screen sheet and @page, keep shadows, gaps, and workspace screen-only, and use a fluid shadowless mobile layout unless a fixed preview is explicitly requested.
Before delivering a document or presentation, render relevant formats and review overflow, proximity of related elements, hierarchy, orphaned headings, clipped blocks, and pagination balance.
